public_comments.comment_text: The court’s permanent orders rewarded obstruction and parental alienation rather than protecting and restoring the father-child relationship. Despite repeated evidence of denied phone calls, withheld parenting time, gatekeeping, scheduling conflicts placed over parenting time, and lack of cooperation from the mother, the Court still awarded her sole decision-making authority over medical, education, therapy, extracurricular activities, and major parenting decisions. The Court relied heavily on historical domestic violence allegations even after the permanent protection order was denied and replaced with only a mutual limited-contact order, using those same allegations to justify denying equal parenting time and joint decision-making. The Court also criticized the lack of family therapy while ignoring that a restraining order and communication barriers made family therapy difficult to initiate, and that the children’s therapists and related recommendations were not meaningfully considered. AppClose communications were used against the father despite his efforts to document concerns professionally, while the mother’s withholding, interference, and controlling behavior were largely minimized. Independent third-party witness testimony, subcontractor financial records, therapist concerns, and corroborating statements were discounted or ignored, while the Court accepted the mother’s narrative with little accountability placed on her conduct. The result was reduced parenting time, removal of midweek parenting, sole decision-making to the parent creating barriers, and financial orders built on unsupported credibility findings rather than balanced evidence and the best interests of the children.
